issues.legal_issue: A testamentary direction requiring heirs who receive property to make continuing charitable payments from its income creates a trust rather than merely a charge when the testator intended to secure a permanent charitable purpose.
material_facts: The will provided that, if the testator and his nephew died without issue, the testator’s legal heirs would receive the property subject to payment of half its net income to a charitable institution or its successor.
The payments were directed to fund specified charitable purposes, including school fees for indigent boys and scholarships.
The amount payable would vary with the property’s net income, and the charity was intended to continue permanently.
The charitable institution applied under section 10 of the Official Trustees Act, 1913, for appointment of an Official Trustee; the heirs contended that the will created only a charge.
issues.conclusion: The heirs held the property subject to a trust for the charitable purposes, rather than merely a charge in favour of the charitable institution; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Whether a direction creates a trust or a charge depends on the testator’s intention gathered from a fair reading of the document and its circumstances; no technical words are necessary. A charge may create a trust where its nature and context impose a fiduciary obligation, particularly where property is subject to continuing payments for charity. The Court applied section 10 of the Official Trustees Act, 1913, and referred to The Commissioners of Charitable Donations and Bequests v. Wybrants (1845) 69 R.R. 278 and Bailey v. Ekins, 7 Ves. 319.

rule.if: will_interpretation_case and property_given_to_heirs and recurring_charitable_income_payment and specified_charitable_purpose and permanent_charitable_intent

predicates.will_interpretation_case: The proceeding requires the court to construe a will to determine the legal effect of a direction concerning property.
predicates.property_given_to_heirs: The will gives property to heirs subject to a direction concerning payments from that property or its income.
predicates.recurring_charitable_income_payment: The will directs the recipients of the property to make continuing payments to a charitable recipient from the property’s income.
predicates.specified_charitable_purpose: The will directs that the payments be used for identified charitable purposes.
predicates.permanent_charitable_intent: The will shows an intention that the charitable provision continue permanently.

issues.definition: When a will-construction proceeding concerns property given to heirs subject to continuing income payments for specified charitable purposes intended to endure permanently, the rule treats the arrangement as a charitable trust.
